datasets.title: DCM
datasets.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
datasets.population: Nonsyndromic DCM probands in published screening series
datasets.denominator: DCM cases, including those without a molecular diagnosis
datasets.caveat: Preliminary estimates from multiple screening series, not one pooled cohort. Referral patterns, ancestry and variant interpretation affect the yield. Syndromic DCM is outside this estimate.

sources.label: GeneReviews · DCM, Table 2
sources.detail: Nonsyndromic Dilated Cardiomyopathy Genes; frequency column and footnote 2. These estimates do not replace current gene–disease validity curation.

entries.note: Truncating variants; exon and transcript context matters.
DCM estimates must be interpreted with variant mechanism.

datasets.title: HCM
datasets.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
datasets.denominator: Genetically solved HCM cases, not all HCM patients
datasets.caveat: These are contributions to positive molecular diagnoses. They are not the chance of a positive test in any HCM patient. Studies and testing eras differ; LVH phenocopies such as Fabry disease and amyloidosis are excluded.

sources.label: GeneReviews · HCM, Table 1
sources.detail: Nonsyndromic HCM overview, updated 6 March 2025; prevalence estimates and footnotes.

sources.label: Alfares et al. · Genetics in Medicine, 2015
sources.detail: Clinical testing of 2,912 HCM probands. Figure 2a describes relative contributions among positive cases; MYBPC3 and MYH7 together accounted for 83% of positive results.

datasets.title: Early-onset AF
datasets.name: Atrial fibrillation · early onset
datasets.metric: Patients with a P/LP finding in each gene
datasets.population: 1,293 patients with AF onset before age 66; 95.7% White
datasets.denominator: All 1,293 tested patients in this early-onset AF cohort
datasets.caveat: P/LP means pathogenic or likely pathogenic. A cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia gene finding does not establish that it caused AF. This selected, predominantly European-ancestry cohort does not estimate gene frequencies in general AF. Only catalog genes with verified carrier counts are shown; VUS are excluded.

sources.label: Yoneda et al. · JAMA Cardiology, 2021
sources.detail: Early-Onset Atrial Fibrillation and the Prevalence of Rare Variants in Cardiomyopathy and Arrhythmia Genes. 1,293 participants; 131 (10.1%) had a disease-associated variant.

sources.label: Yoneda et al. · cohort follow-up, 2022
sources.detail: Mortality Among Patients With Early-Onset AF and Rare Variants in Cardiomyopathy and Arrhythmia Genes. Confirms patient carrier counts: TTN 38, MYH7 18, LMNA 9, KCNQ1 8. Percentages here are calculated against the original 1,293 tested patients, not mortality outcomes.

datasets.title: Long QT syndrome
datasets.name: Arrhythmia · long QT syndrome
datasets.denominator: LQTS cases, including those without an identified genetic cause
datasets.caveat: Arrhythmia frequencies are syndrome specific. These estimates cannot be applied to all ventricular arrhythmia, acquired QT prolongation, AF or other SCN5A phenotypes. Rare overlap syndromes require variant- and inheritance-specific review.

sources.label: GeneReviews · LQTS, Table 4
sources.detail: Long QT Syndrome: Genetic Causes, updated 21 March 2024. Proportion attributed to pathogenic variants; not penetrance or cardiac-event rates.

entries.note: Gain-of-function; Timothy syndrome context may apply.

datasets.title: CPVT
datasets.name: Arrhythmia · CPVT
datasets.denominator: CPVT cases, including those without an identified genetic cause
datasets.caveat: These are CPVT-specific estimates, not frequencies across all ventricular arrhythmias. Most CASQ2 disease is recessive; rare dominant variants require separate interpretation. RYR2 variant mechanism also matters.

sources.label: GeneReviews · CPVT, Table 1
sources.detail: Proportion of CPVT attributed to pathogenic variants in each gene. The separate assay detection-rate columns are not used.

entries.note: Usually autosomal recessive; rare dominant variants.

datasets.title: Brugada syndrome
datasets.name: Arrhythmia · Brugada syndrome
datasets.caveat: The 2022 ESC guideline identifies SCN5A as the gene with established evidence for Brugada syndrome. Historical candidate genes are not ranked here. The estimate is neither SCN5A penetrance nor a percentage of all ventricular arrhythmia.

sources.label: ESC ventricular arrhythmia guideline · 2022
sources.detail: Brugada syndrome section: genetic testing yield approximately 20%, with SCN5A the gene supported by clinical association evidence.

datasets.title: HTAD referrals
datasets.name: Thoracic aortic disease · referral cohort
datasets.metric: Patients with a P/LP sequence finding
datasets.population: 810 Dutch index patients referred for suspected heritable thoracic aortic disorders, 2015–2017
datasets.denominator: All 810 tested index patients, including negative results
datasets.coverageNote: Sequence variant findings only. Six additional copy-number diagnoses are outside these rows.
datasets.caveat: This mixed referral cohort is not a familial-only, Marfan-only or vascular Ehlers–Danlos cohort, and does not represent all aortic disease. Rows use the 60 sequence-variant diagnoses over all 810 referrals. Six further CNV diagnoses were reported separately and are excluded from these gene counts; VUS are excluded. Test selection, age and the 2015–2017 assay affect yield. Genes outside the study panel have no estimate here.

sources.label: Overwater et al. · Human Mutation, 2018
sources.detail: Results section 3.1 gives gene-specific counts for 60 sequence-variant-positive patients among 810 index referrals. A separate six CNV diagnoses bring the overall study yield to 66/810. The per-gene percentages in the article use 60 positives; this app recalculates against all 810 referrals.

datasets.title: Loeys–Dietz syndrome
datasets.name: Loeys–Dietz syndrome
datasets.population: Patients with Loeys–Dietz syndrome in the GeneReviews reference summary
datasets.denominator: Loeys–Dietz syndrome cases, not all aortic disease patients
datasets.coverageNote: Catalog genes only; IPO8 is outside this panel. Ranges are independent estimates.
datasets.caveat: These syndrome-specific estimates cannot be applied to nonsyndromic thoracic aortic disease, Marfan syndrome or vascular Ehlers–Danlos syndrome. The contribution column is used, not the separate assay detection-rate columns. The catalog does not contain IPO8. Published ranges overlap and must not be added to predict panel yield.

sources.label: GeneReviews · Loeys–Dietz syndrome, Table 1
sources.detail: Updated 12 September 2024. Proportion of LDS attributed to pathogenic variants in each gene; footnote 3 cites Meester et al. 2017. Sequence-analysis detection rates are separate and are not ranked here.

datasets.title: Familial PAH
datasets.name: PAH · familial
datasets.metric: Estimated BMPR2 contribution to familial PAH
datasets.population: Patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension occurring in families
datasets.denominator: Familial PAH cases, including those without a molecular diagnosis
datasets.coverageNote: BMPR2 has a curated range here. Other PAH genes are not assigned an invented percentage.
datasets.caveat: This literature range applies to familial pulmonary arterial hypertension, not all pulmonary hypertension or all genetically diagnosed PAH. It is not the probability that a healthy BMPR2 carrier develops PAH. Associated PAH, idiopathic PAH and PVOD/PCH have different gene distributions. Rare-gene estimates vary by cohort, ancestry and age.

sources.label: Zhu et al. · Genome Medicine, 2019
sources.detail: Background: BMPR2 variants reported in 60–80% of familial PAH. The separate PAH Biobank research-variant counts are not used as clinical P/LP frequencies here.

sources.label: International PAH genetic testing consensus · 2023
sources.detail: Distinguishes familial, idiopathic and PVOD/PCH disease. The quoted 70–87% familial yield in its text is for all known PAH genes, not BMPR2 alone.

datasets.title: Idiopathic PAH
datasets.name: PAH · idiopathic
datasets.metric: Estimated BMPR2 contribution to idiopathic PAH
datasets.population: PAH cases without an identified associated cause or recognized family history before testing
datasets.denominator: Clinically idiopathic PAH cases before genetic classification
datasets.caveat: This literature range describes clinically idiopathic PAH before genetic testing. A pathogenic finding can subsequently reclassify a case as heritable PAH. It does not apply to all pulmonary hypertension, and is not a penetrance estimate. Broader cohorts, ancestries and testing strategies have reported different yields.

sources.label: The role of genomics and genetics in PAH · 2020
sources.detail: Published synthesis reports BMPR2 variants in approximately 10–20% of idiopathic PAH; kept separate from its familial PAH estimates.

sources.label: International PAH genetic testing consensus · 2023
sources.detail: Distinguishes familial, idiopathic and PVOD/PCH disease. The quoted 70–87% familial yield in its text is for all known PAH genes, not BMPR2 alone.

datasets.title: Sporadic PVOD
datasets.name: PVOD · sporadic discovery cohort
datasets.population: 20 histologically confirmed, apparently sporadic PVOD cases in the discovery study
datasets.denominator: All 20 sporadic PVOD patients tested in this study
datasets.caveat: This small, selected discovery cohort is not an estimate for all PAH, all pulmonary hypertension or all PVOD/PCH populations. Both EIF2AK4 alleles must be considered. A single heterozygous finding is not equivalent to the biallelic disease counted here. Familial PVOD uses a separate family-based denominator.

sources.label: Eyries et al. · Nature Genetics, 2014
sources.detail: Biallelic EIF2AK4 findings in 13 of 13 studied PVOD families and 5 of 20 histologically confirmed sporadic PVOD cases. Families and individual patients are separate denominators.

entries.note: Biallelic findings only; selected histology-confirmed cohort.

datasets.title: Familial PVOD
datasets.name: PVOD · familial discovery cohort
datasets.metric: Studied families with biallelic EIF2AK4 findings
datasets.population: 13 selected PVOD families in the original discovery study
datasets.denominator: All 13 PVOD families studied, not 13 individual patients
datasets.coverageNote: 13/13 studied families is a discovery-series observation, not universal test sensitivity.
datasets.caveat: All 13 families in this selected discovery study had biallelic EIF2AK4 findings. This does not establish 100% sensitivity in other PVOD populations, and must not be applied to all pulmonary hypertension. The unit is families, not patients. Sporadic PVOD is shown separately.

sources.label: Eyries et al. · Nature Genetics, 2014
sources.detail: Biallelic EIF2AK4 findings in 13 of 13 studied PVOD families and 5 of 20 histologically confirmed sporadic PVOD cases. Families and individual patients are separate denominators.

entries.note: Biallelic findings; selected families, not population prevalence.

datasets.title: Familial hypercholesterolemia
datasets.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH)
datasets.population: Probands with a clinical diagnosis of familial hypercholesterolemia
datasets.denominator: Clinically diagnosed FH cases, including genetically unresolved cases
datasets.coverageNote: ABCG5, ABCG8, APOE and LIPA represent other lipid disorders; FH percentages are not assigned to them.
datasets.caveat: These estimates apply to clinical FH, not all elevated cholesterol or dyslipidemia. Clinical criteria, age, ancestry and founder variants affect yield. LDLR >50% is a lower bound, not an exact percentage or an assay detection rate. PCSK9 estimates concern gain-of-function disease. Sitosterolemia, dysbetalipoproteinemia and lysosomal acid lipase deficiency need separate disease-specific estimates.

sources.label: GeneReviews · FH, Table 1
sources.detail: Uses the proportion of FH attributed to pathogenic variants: LDLR >50%, APOB approximately 5–10%, PCSK9 <1%, LDLRAP1 <1%. Footnote 7 cites Sturm et al. 2018. Sequence-analysis and deletion/duplication detection-rate columns are not used.

entries.note: Lower bound; sequence and copy-number analysis are relevant.
